Ever wonder why a traditional PostgreSQL setup struggles with AI workloads?
I read the Nebius announcement about their new Managed PostgreSQL for AI.
They designed it to handle large embedding tables,
 low‑latency queries,
 and dynamic scaling.
In my own projects, I’ve seen vector extensions double query speed,
 but managing the hardware was a headache.
Nebius’s managed service takes care of the heavy lifting,
 so you can focus on model fine‑tuning instead of cluster ops.
Here are a few practical takeaways:
- Built‑in vector extensions let you store embeddings directly in the database.
- Automatic scaling adjusts resources as your inference load spikes,
 keeping latency low.
- Continuous backups and point‑in‑time recovery protect you during long training runs.
If you’re already using PostgreSQL, consider testing the managed offering on a pilot model.
It could save weeks of engineering time and give you more predictable performance.
What challenges have you faced when scaling databases for AI,
 and how did you solve them?
#PostgreSQL #AI #DataEngineering #ManagedServices

news_posts.post_content:
Ever notice how a single query can stall an entire pipeline?
I was digging into a recent DBtune release and saw they added autonomous optimization for PostgreSQL.
The tool monitors query patterns,
adjusts planner settings,
and even rewrites indexes on the fly.
In my last project the same bottleneck took days to tune manually.
After plugging in DBtune,
the same workload ran 40% faster within hours.
It feels like having a DBA that never sleeps.
Here are a few things I tried that made a difference:
- Let DBtune run its baseline analysis before any major ETL run.
- Review the suggested index changes and apply them in a staging environment first.
- Use the auto‑tune schedule during off‑peak hours to avoid surprise plan shifts.
A couple of cautions:
- Keep an eye on the generated plans;
sometimes the optimizer picks a plan that looks good on paper but hurts a specific workload.
- Make sure your Postgres version is compatible with the DBtune agent.
Overall,
autonomous tuning feels like a safety net for performance hiccups.
What’s your experience with self‑tuning tools in production?
#PostgreSQL #DBtune #DataEngineering #Performance
